Resolver Architecture
=====================

Fromager resolves package versions from multiple sources using a
provider abstraction.  This document describes the resolution
strategies, filtering, and key design decisions.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.
   :doc:`bootstrapper-architecture` covers how resolution fits into the
   bootstrap pipeline.

Resolution Strategies
---------------------

During bootstrap, the resolver coordinator tries these sources in
priority order and accumulates results in a thread-safe session cache:

.. code-block:: text

   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │               Resolution Priority Order               │
   │                                                       │
   │  1. Session cache (versions found earlier)            │
   │          │ miss                                       │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  2. Previous dependency graph (prior run)             │
   │          │ miss                                       │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  3. Network (PyPI / GitHub / GitLab)                  │
   │     (per-package configurable)                        │
   │          │ age filter empties result                  │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  4. Cache server fallback                             │
   │     (multiple_versions mode only)                     │
   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

   Git URL requirements (top-level only) bypass this
   chain entirely: the repo is cloned and the version
   is extracted from package metadata.

Versions discovered from any source are merged into the session cache.
Subsequent requests for the same package skip the network entirely if
the cache already contains a matching version.

Provider Hierarchy
------------------

All resolution sources inherit from ``BaseProvider``, which implements
the resolvelib ``ExtrasProvider`` interface.  The bootstrap engine and
CLI commands interact with providers through a common
``find_matches()`` method.

.. code-block:: text

   BaseProvider
   ├── PyPIProvider         (PEP 503 Simple API)
   │   └── PyPICacheProvider  (fromager's own wheel server)
   ├── GenericProvider      (callback-based, parses tags)
   │   ├── GitHubTagProvider
   │   └── GitLabTagProvider
   └── VersionMapProvider   (pre-resolved version→URL map)

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 75

   * - Provider
     - What it queries
   * - ``PyPIProvider``
     - Any PEP 503 Simple API index (pypi.org, custom mirrors).
       Filters by platform tags, Python version, and yanked status.
   * - ``PyPICacheProvider``
     - Subclass of ``PyPIProvider`` pointing at fromager's own wheel
       server.  No cooldown applied.  Used as a fallback when age
       filtering eliminates all candidates.
   * - ``GenericProvider``
     - Callback-based provider that pairs a version source function
       with a configurable match function (plain parse or regex).
       Base class for the tag providers below.
   * - ``GitHubTagProvider``
     - GitHub REST API for repository tags.  Versions are parsed
       from tag names using a configurable pattern.
   * - ``GitLabTagProvider``
     - GitLab REST API for repository tags.  Includes upload
       timestamps for age filtering.
   * - ``VersionMapProvider``
     - Wraps a pre-built ``VersionMap`` (version → URL mapping).
       Used when versions are already known, e.g. from a prior
       resolution or a settings-provided URL template.

Per-package settings in YAML can select which provider to use and
configure its parameters (index URL, tag pattern, etc.).  Override
plugins can replace the provider entirely for a specific package via
the ``get_resolver_provider`` hook.

Version Filtering Window
-------------------------

Two age-based filters can narrow the set of acceptable versions:

.. code-block:: text

   ◄── too old ──┤  acceptable window  ├── too new ──►

                 │                      │
            max_age cutoff         cooldown cutoff
          (reject before this)   (reject after this)

- **Cooldown** rejects releases that are too new.  It ensures a
  minimum time has passed since publication, guarding against
  problematic releases.  Configurable per package; bypassed for
  exact version pins (``==``).

- **Max age** rejects releases that are too old.  Used primarily in
  ``multiple_versions`` mode to limit the range of versions built.
  Packages with a constraint in the provider's constraints bypass this
  filter, including both exact pins and version ranges.

  .. versionchanged:: unreleased
     Constrained packages skip max-age filtering in both resolution modes.

When both are active, only versions published within the window are
considered.  If all candidates are filtered out, the behavior depends
on the mode: in single-version mode a warning is logged and all
candidates are kept; in ``multiple_versions`` mode the cache server
fallback is tried instead.

Flat Resolution by Design
-------------------------

Fromager deliberately does **not** use resolvelib's transitive
dependency resolution.  Every provider's ``get_dependencies()`` method
returns an empty list.  This means resolution is a simple "find the
best matching version" operation, not a full constraint solver with
backtracking.

Transitive dependencies are handled by the bootstrap engine's own DFS
loop: after a package is built, its install dependencies are extracted
from the wheel metadata and pushed onto the work stack as new
``RESOLVE`` phase items.  This separation keeps the resolver stateless
and makes each resolution call independent and thread-safe.

Per-Package Configuration
-------------------------

Package settings files (YAML) can configure the resolver for each
package independently: resolver type (PyPI, GitHub tags, GitLab tags,
hook-based, or blocked), index URL, cooldown, tag pattern, and
override plugins.

See :doc:`package-settings` for how settings are loaded and merged.

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=200)
def match_py_req(py_req: str, *, python_version: Version = PYTHON_VERSION) -> bool:
    """Python version requirement lookup with LRU cache

    Raises InvalidSpecifier on error

    SpecifierSet parsing and matching takes a non-trivial amount of time. A
    bootstrap run can spend over 10% of its time in parsing and matching
    Python version requirements.

    This function caches the result of SpecifierSet parsing and contains
    operation for Python version requirement. Most packages share similar
    constraints, e.g. ``>= 3.10``.
    """
    return python_version in SpecifierSet(py_req)


def resolve(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool = True,
    include_wheels: bool = True,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, Version]:
    """Resolve requirement and return the best matching version.

    Returns (url, version) tuple for the highest matching version.
    """
    # Create the (reusable) resolver.
    provider = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_resolver_provider",
        default_resolver_provider,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )
    provider.cooldown = resolve_package_cooldown(ctx, req, req_type=req_type)
    max_age_cutoff = _compute_max_age_cutoff(ctx)
    results = find_all_matching_from_provider(
        provider, req, max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff
    )
    return results[0]


def default_resolver_provider(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool,
    include_wheels: bool,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> (
    PyPIProvider
    | GenericProvider
    | GitHubTagProvider
    | GitLabTagProvider
    | VersionMapProvider
):
    """Lookup resolver provider to resolve package versions"""
    return PyPIProvider(
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        constraints=ctx.constraints,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )


def _has_equality_pin(req: Requirement) -> bool:
    """Return True if the requirement has a single exact ``==`` pin.

    Rejects wildcard pins (``==1.*``) and compound specifiers (``==1,>2``)
    which are not true exact version pins.
    """
    specs = list(req.specifier)
    return len(specs) == 1 and specs[0].operator == "==" and "*" not in specs[0].version


def resolve_package_cooldown(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
) -> Cooldown | None:
    """Compute the effective cooldown for a single package.

    Args:
        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).
        req: The package requirement being resolved.
        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).

    Returns:
        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.
    """
    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):
        if ctx.cooldown is not None:
            logger.info("cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin")
        return None

    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age
    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown
    if per_package_days is None:
        return global_cooldown
    if per_package_days == 0:
        return None
    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all
    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.
    bootstrap_time = (
        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time
        if global_cooldown is not None
        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )
    return Cooldown(
        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),
        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,
    )

Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. This is safe because get_dependencies() returns []\n        # (no transitive deps to resolve). If get_dependencies() is ever extended,\n        # this must be revisited to use resolvelib's full resolution.\n        candidates = provider.find_matches(\n            identifier=identifier,\n            requirements={identifier: [req]},\n            incompatibilities={},  # Empty - safe only because no transitive deps\n        )\n    except resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException as err:\n        constraint = provider.constraints.get_constraint(req.name)\n        provider_desc = provider.get_provider_description()\n        original_msg = str(err)\n        raise resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException(\n            f\"Unable to resolve requirement specifier {req} with constraint {constraint} using {provider_desc}: {original_msg}\"\n        ) from err\n\n    # Materialize candidates so we can iterate more than once if filtering\n    candidates_list = list(candidates)\n\n    if max_age_cutoff is not None:\n        logger.info(\n            \"%s: found %d candidate(s) matching %s\",\n            req.name,\n            len(candidates_list),\n            req,\n        )\n        max_age_days = (datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC) - self.add_constraint(line)\n\n    def dump_constraints(self, output: typing.TextIO) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Dump combined constraints to a text stream\"\"\"\n        # sort by normalized name\n        for _, req in sorted(self._data.items()):\n            # write requirement without markers. They have been evaluated\n            # in add_constraint()\n            output.write(f\"{req.name}{req.specifier}\\n\")\n\n    def get_constraint(self, name: str) -> Requirement | None:\n """Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import (
    candidate,
    constraints,
    context,
    packagesettings,
    resolver,
    sources,
    wheels,
)
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)
_cooldown_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "ccc"},
            "upload-time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_all_recent_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-25T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_COOLDOWN = candidate.Cooldown(
    min_age=_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS,
    bootstrap_time=_BOOTSTRAP_TIME,
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.
    """
    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:
    """Without a cooldown the resolver selects the latest version as normal."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=None)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"


def test_cooldown_all_blocked_raises_informative_error() -> None:
    """When all candidates are within the cooldown window the error says so."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_all_recent_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())

        with pytest.raises(resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException) as exc_info:
            rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "2 candidate(s)" in msg
        assert "published within the last 7 days (release-age cooldown" in msg


def test_cooldown_rejects_candidate_without_upload_time(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A candidate with no upload_time is rejected when a cooldown is active (fail closed)."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    candidate = resolver.Candidate(
        name="test-pkg",
        version=Version("1.0.0"),
        url="https://example.com/test-pkg-1.0.0.tar.gz",
        upload_time=None,
    )
    provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(cooldown=_COOLDOWN)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
        result = provider.is_blocked_by_cooldown(candidate)

    assert result is True
    assert "upload_time unknown" in caplog.text
    assert "1.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_missing_timestamp_error_message() -> None:
    """Resolution failure due to missing timestamps produces a clear error message."""
    no_timestamp_response = {
        "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
        "name": "test-pkg",
        "files": [

                "filename": "test_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
                "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
                "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            },
        ],
    }

Resolver Architecture
=====================

Fromager resolves package versions from multiple sources using a
provider abstraction.  This document describes the resolution
strategies, filtering, and key design decisions.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.
   :doc:`bootstrapper-architecture` covers how resolution fits into the
   bootstrap pipeline.

Resolution Strategies
---------------------

During bootstrap, the resolver coordinator tries these sources in
priority order and accumulates results in a thread-safe session cache:

.. code-block:: text

   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │               Resolution Priority Order               │
   │                                                       │
   │  1. Session cache (versions found earlier)            │
   │          │ miss                                       │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  2. Previous dependency graph (prior run)             │
   │          │ miss                                       │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  3. Network (PyPI / GitHub / GitLab)                  │
   │     (per-package configurable)                        │
   │          │ age filter empties result                  │
   │          ▼                                            │
   │  4. Cache server fallback                             │
   │     (multiple_versions mode only)                     │
   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

   Git URL requirements (top-level only) bypass this
   chain entirely: the repo is cloned and the version
   is extracted from package metadata.

Versions discovered from any source are merged into the session cache.
Subsequent requests for the same package skip the network entirely if
the cache already contains a matching version.

Provider Hierarchy
------------------

All resolution sources inherit from ``BaseProvider``, which implements
the resolvelib ``ExtrasProvider`` interface.  The bootstrap engine and
CLI commands interact with providers through a common
``find_matches()`` method.

.. code-block:: text

   BaseProvider
   ├── PyPIProvider         (PEP 503 Simple API)
   │   └── PyPICacheProvider  (fromager's own wheel server)
   ├── GenericProvider      (callback-based, parses tags)
   │   ├── GitHubTagProvider
   │   └── GitLabTagProvider
   └── VersionMapProvider   (pre-resolved version→URL map)

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 75

   * - Provider
     - What it queries
   * - ``PyPIProvider``
     - Any PEP 503 Simple API index (pypi.org, custom mirrors).
       Filters by platform tags, Python version, and yanked status.
   * - ``PyPICacheProvider``
     - Subclass of ``PyPIProvider`` pointing at fromager's own wheel
       server.  No cooldown applied.  Used as a fallback when age
       filtering eliminates all candidates.
   * - ``GenericProvider``
     - Callback-based provider that pairs a version source function
       with a configurable match function (plain parse or regex).
       Base class for the tag providers below.
   * - ``GitHubTagProvider``
     - GitHub REST API for repository tags.  Versions are parsed
       from tag names using a configurable pattern.
   * - ``GitLabTagProvider``
     - GitLab REST API for repository tags.  Includes upload
       timestamps for age filtering.
   * - ``VersionMapProvider``
     - Wraps a pre-built ``VersionMap`` (version → URL mapping).
       Used when versions are already known, e.g. from a prior
       resolution or a settings-provided URL template.

Per-package settings in YAML can select which provider to use and
configure its parameters (index URL, tag pattern, etc.).  Override
plugins can replace the provider entirely for a specific package via
the ``get_resolver_provider`` hook.

Version Filtering Window
-------------------------

Two age-based filters can narrow the set of acceptable versions:

.. code-block:: text

   ◄── too old ──┤  acceptable window  ├── too new ──►

                 │                      │
            max_age cutoff         cooldown cutoff
          (reject before this)   (reject after this)

- **Cooldown** rejects releases that are too new.  It ensures a
  minimum time has passed since publication, guarding against
  problematic releases.  Configurable per package; bypassed for
  exact version pins (``==``).

- **Max age** rejects releases that are too old.  Used primarily in
  ``multiple_versions`` mode to limit the range of versions built.
  Packages with an explicit constraint bypass this filter, including
  both exact pins and version ranges.  Cooldown still applies independently.

  .. versionchanged:: 0.84.0
     Explicit constraints take precedence over the max-age filter.

When both are active, only versions published within the window are
considered.  If all candidates are filtered out, the behavior depends
on the mode: in single-version mode a warning is logged and all
candidates are kept; in ``multiple_versions`` mode the cache server
fallback is tried instead.

Flat Resolution by Design
-------------------------

Fromager deliberately does **not** use resolvelib's transitive
dependency resolution.  Every provider's ``get_dependencies()`` method
returns an empty list.  This means resolution is a simple "find the
best matching version" operation, not a full constraint solver with
backtracking.

Transitive dependencies are handled by the bootstrap engine's own DFS
loop: after a package is built, its install dependencies are extracted
from the wheel metadata and pushed onto the work stack as new
``RESOLVE`` phase items.  This separation keeps the resolver stateless
and makes each resolution call independent and thread-safe.

Per-Package Configuration
-------------------------

Package settings files (YAML) can configure the resolver for each
package independently: resolver type (PyPI, GitHub tags, GitLab tags,
hook-based, or blocked), index URL, cooldown, tag pattern, and
override plugins.

See :doc:`package-settings` for how settings are loaded and merged.

#
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import functools

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

DEBUG_RESOLVER = os.environ.get("DEBUG_RESOLVER", "")
PYPI_SERVER_URL = "https://pypi.org/simple"
GITHUB_URL = "https://github.com"

# all supported tags
SUPPORTED_TAGS: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(sys_tags())
# same, but ignore the platform for 'ignore_platform' flag
IGNORE_PLATFORM: str = "ignore"
SUPPORTED_TAGS_IGNORE_PLATFORM: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(
    Tag(t.interpreter, t.abi, IGNORE_PLATFORM) for t in SUPPORTED_TAGS
)


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=200)
def match_py_req(py_req: str, *, python_version: Version = PYTHON_VERSION) -> bool:
    """Python version requirement lookup with LRU cache

    Raises InvalidSpecifier on error

    SpecifierSet parsing and matching takes a non-trivial amount of time. A
    bootstrap run can spend over 10% of its time in parsing and matching
    Python version requirements.

    This function caches the result of SpecifierSet parsing and contains
    operation for Python version requirement. Most packages share similar
    constraints, e.g. ``>= 3.10``.
    """
    return python_version in SpecifierSet(py_req)


def resolve(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool = True,
    include_wheels: bool = True,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, Version]:
    """Resolve requirement and return the best matching version.

    Returns (url, version) tuple for the highest matching version.
    """
    # Create the (reusable) resolver.
    provider = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_resolver_provider",
        default_resolver_provider,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )
    provider.cooldown = resolve_package_cooldown(ctx, req, req_type=req_type)
    max_age_cutoff = _compute_max_age_cutoff(ctx)
    results = find_all_matching_from_provider(
        provider, req, max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff
    )
    return results[0]


def default_resolver_provider(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool,
    include_wheels: bool,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> (
    PyPIProvider
    | GenericProvider
    | GitHubTagProvider
    | GitLabTagProvider
    | VersionMapProvider
):
    """Lookup resolver provider to resolve package versions"""
    return PyPIProvider(
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        constraints=ctx.constraints,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )


def _has_equality_pin(req: Requirement) -> bool:
    """Return True if the requirement has a single exact ``==`` pin.

    Rejects wildcard pins (``==1.*``) and compound specifiers (``==1,>2``)
    which are not true exact version pins.
    """
    specs = list(req.specifier)
    return len(specs) == 1 and specs[0].operator == "==" and "*" not in specs[0].version


def resolve_package_cooldown(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
) -> Cooldown | None:
    """Compute the effective cooldown for a single package.

    Args:
        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).
        req: The package requirement being resolved.
        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).

    Returns:
        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.
    """
    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):
        if ctx.cooldown is not None:
            logger.info("cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin")
        return None

    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age
    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown
    if per_package_days is None:
        return global_cooldown
    if per_package_days == 0:
        return None
    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all
    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.
    bootstrap_time = (
        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time
        if global_cooldown is not None
        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )
    return Cooldown(
        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),
        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,
    )

...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never Stop when failure is fixed and regression proof passes.\n---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Constraints with\n           conflicts now raise :exc:`InvalidConstraintError`. Inputs without a\n           version specifier or with extras are also refused.\n        \"\"\"\n        req = Requirement(unparsed)\n        canon_name = canonicalize_name(req.name)\n        previous = self._data.get(canon_name)\n\n        # validator properties: must have a specifier, must not have extras or URL\n        if req.extras:\n            raise InvalidConstraintError(f\"Constraint {unparsed!r} has extras\")\n        if req.url:\n            raise InvalidConstraintError(f\"Constraint {unparsed!r} has a URL\")\n        if not req.specifier:\n            raise InvalidConstraintError(f\"Constraint {unparsed!r} has no specifiers\")\n\n        # A \"blocked\" specifier (<0, <0.0, <0.0.0) is intentionally\n        # unsatisfiable and used to exclude a package from builds.\n        blocked = _is_blocked_specifier(req.specifier)\n\n        # verify that incoming constraint is okay by itself\n        if not blocked and req.specifier.is_unsatisfiable():\n            raise InvalidConstraintError(f\"Constraint {unparsed!r} is unsatisfiable\")\n\n        if not requirements_file.evaluate_marker(req, req):\n            logger.debug(f\"Constraint {req} does not match environment\")\n            return\n\n        if previous is not None:\n            prev_blocked = _is_blocked_specifier(previous.specifier)\n            if blocked != prev_blocked:\n                raise InvalidConstraintError(\n                    f\"Cannot combine blocked and non-blocked constraints \"\n                    f\"(existing: {previous}, new: {req})\"\n                )\n            if not blocked:\n                logger.debug(\"combining constraints %s and %s\", previous, req)\n                new_specifier = req.specifier & previous.specifier\n                if new_specifier.is_unsatisfiable():\n                    raise InvalidConstraintError(\n                        f\"Combined specifier '{new_specifier}' is not satisfiable \"\n                        f\"(existing: {previous}, new: {req})\"\n                    )\n                req.specifier = new_specifier\n        else:\n            logger.debug(f\"adding constraint {req}\")\n\n        self._data[canon_name] = req\n\n    def load_constraints_file(self, constraints_file: str | pathlib.Path) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Load constraints from a constraints file or URL\"\"\"\n        logger.info(\"loading constraints from %s\", constraints_file)\n        content = requirements_file.parse_requirements_file(constraints_file)\n        for line in content:\n            self.add_constraint(line)\n\n    def dump_constraints(self, output: typing.TextIO) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Dump combined constraints to a text stream\"\"\"\n        # sort by normalized name\n        for _, req in sorted(self._data.items()):\n            # write requirement without markers. They have been evaluated\n            # in add_constraint()\n            output.write(f\"{req.name}{req.specifier}\\n\")\n\n    def get_constraint(self, name: str) -> Requirement | None:\n        return self._data.get(canonicalize_name(name))\n\n    def allow_prerelease(self, pkg_name: str) -> bool:\n        constraint = self.get_constraint(pkg_name)\n        if constraint:\n            return bool(constraint.specifier.prereleases)\n        return False\n\n    def is_blocked(self, pkg_name: str) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Return True if the package is blocked by a ``<0`` constraint.\"\"\"\n        constraint = self.get_constraint(pkg_name)\n        if constraint:\n            return _is_blocked_specifier(constraint.specifier)\n        return False\n\n    def is_satisfied_by(self, pkg_name: str, version: Version) -> bool:\n        constraint = self.get_constraint(pkg_name)\n        if constraint:\n            return constraint.specifier.contains(version, prereleases=True)\n        return True\n\nTwo age-based filters can narrow the set of acceptable versions:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   ◄── too old ──┤  acceptable window  ├── too new ──►\n\n                 │                      │\n            max_age cutoff         cooldown cutoff\n          (reject before this)   (reject after this)\n\n- **Cooldown** rejects releases that are too new.  It ensures a\n  minimum time has passed since publication, guarding against\n  problematic releases.  Configurable per package; bypassed for\n  exact version pins (``==``).\n\n- **Max age** rejects releases that are too old.  Used primarily in\n  ``multiple_versions`` mode to limit the range of versions built.\n\nWhen both are active, only versions published within the window are\nconsidered.  If all candidates are filtered out, the behavior depends\non the mode: in single-version mode a warning is logged and all\ncandidates are kept; in ``multiple_versions`` mode the cache server\nfallback is tried instead.\n\nFlat Resolution by Design\n-------------------------\n\nFromager deliberately does **not** use resolvelib's transitive\n13:dynamic = [\"version\"]\n119:lint = \"fromager.commands.lint:lint\"\n121:list-versions = \"fromager.commands.list_versions:list_versions\"\n130:lint-requirements = \"fromager.commands.lint_requirements:lint_requirements\"\n151:[tool.hatch.version]\n152:path = \"src/fromager/version.py\"\n159:target-version = \"py312\"\n163:    \"src/fromager/version.py\", # file is generated dynamically, out of our control\n166:[tool.ruff.lint]\n189:[tool.ruff.lint.isort]\n226:# No specific python version here, so it uses the active Python by default.\n239:[tool.hatch.envs.lint]\n240:description = \"Run linters.\"\n241:skip-install = true # Corresponds to skipping project installation for linting\n246:  \"check-python-versions\",\n249:[tool.hatch.envs.lint.scripts]\n253:  \"python ./e2e/mergify_lint.py\",\n255:fix = [\n261:pkglint = [\n264:  \"check-python-versions --only pyproject.toml,.github/workflows/test.yaml\",\n267:mergify = \"python ./e2e/mergify_lint.py\"\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

"""Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import candidate, context, packagesettings, resolver, sources, wheels
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)
_cooldown_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "ccc"},
            "upload-time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_all_recent_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-25T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_COOLDOWN = candidate.Cooldown(
    min_age=_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS,
    bootstrap_time=_BOOTSTRAP_TIME,
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.
    """
    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:
    """Without a cooldown the resolver selects the latest version as normal."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=None)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"


def test_cooldown_all_blocked_raises_informative_error() -> None:
    """When all candidates are within the cooldown window the error says so."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_all_recent_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())

        with pytest.raises(resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException) as exc_info:
            rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "2 candidate(s)" in msg
        assert "published within the last 7 days (release-age cooldown" in msg


def test_cooldown_rejects_candidate_without_upload_time(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A candidate with no upload_time is rejected when a cooldown is active (fail closed)."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    candidate = resolver.Candidate(
        name="test-pkg",
        version=Version("1.0.0"),
        url="https://example.com/test-pkg-1.0.0.tar.gz",
        upload_time=None,
    )
    provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(cooldown=_COOLDOWN)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
        result = provider.is_blocked_by_cooldown(candidate)

    assert result is True
    assert "upload_time unknown" in caplog.text
    assert "1.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_missing_timestamp_error_message() -> None:
    """Resolution failure due to missing timestamps produces a clear error message."""
    no_timestamp_response = {
        "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
        "name": "test-pkg",
        "files": [
            {
                "filename": "test_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
                "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
                "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},

        ],

            json=no_timestamp_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)

A virtualenv with the project\nand test dependencies is already set up at `.venv`; run tests with\n`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts=\"\" tests/...`.\n\nIssue #1214: fromager might \"lie\" about the reason of a dependency resolution failure\n\n> Expected: fromager states the exact reason of the broken dependency chain.\n> Actual: with ENABLE_REPEATABLE_BUILD_MODE and a broken indirect dependency, the error is\n> logged under whatever top-level package is active in the logging context, e.g.\n> `ERROR its-hub: Unable to resolve requirement specifier flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1 ...`\n> while the real chain is its-hub -> reward-hub -> vllm and vllm is the broken arc.\n> fromager should say the resolution is broken because of vllm, not its-hub.\n\nFix it in the iterative bootstrapper (`src/fromager/bootstrapper/_bootstrapper.py`).\nDesign agreed in review:\n\n- Add `Bootstrapper._dependency_chain_suffix(self, wi: WorkItem)\
  \ -> str` returning\n  `\" (dependency chain: a==1 -> b==2 -> <wi.req>)\"` built from `wi.why_snapshot`\n  (each entry is `(_, req, version)`, rendered as `req.name==version`).\n- Add `Bootstrapper._enrich_resolution_error(self, item: Phase, err: Exception) -> Exception`.\n  For a `Resolve` phase item whose work item has a non-empty `why_snapshot`, return a\n  new exception of the same shape with the chain suffix appended to the message:\n  `resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException` stays a `ResolverException`, `RuntimeError`\n  stays a `RuntimeError`, anything else becomes `RuntimeError(\"<TypeName>: <msg><suffix>\")`.\n  For other phases or top-level requirements return `err` unchanged (same object).\n- `_handle_phase_error()` must raise the enriched exception without a `from` clause,\n  still inside the original handler, so the original is reachable via `__context__`\n  but `__cause__` stays unset (the top-level formatter follows `__cause__` and would\n  otherwise print the message twice).\
  \ Enrichment must happen before the error is\n  recorded in test mode or multiple-versions mode, and before the normal-mode raise.\n\nAdd tests to `tests/test_bootstrapper_iterative.py` and run that file.\n"

    bootstrap_requirement_resolver,

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class Bootstrapper:
    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        progressbar: progress.Progressbar | None = None,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str | None = None,
        sdist_only: bool = False,
        test_mode: bool = False,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        num_bg_threads: int = _DEFAULT_BG_THREADS,
    ) -> None:
        if test_mode and sdist_only:
            raise ValueError(
                "--test-mode requires full wheel builds; incompatible with --sdist-only"
            )

        self.ctx = ctx
        self.progressbar = progressbar or progress.Progressbar(None)
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url or ctx.wheel_server_url
        self.sdist_only = sdist_only
        self.test_mode = test_mode
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.why: list[tuple[RequirementType, Requirement, Version]] = []
        self._num_bg_threads = max(1, num_bg_threads)
        self._bg_pool: concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor | None = (
            concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(
                max_workers=self._num_bg_threads, thread_name_prefix="fromager-bg"
            )
        )

        # Delegate resolution to BootstrapRequirementResolver
        self._resolver = bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver(
            ctx=ctx,
            prev_graph=prev_graph,
            multiple_versions=multiple_versions,
            cache_wheel_server_url=self.cache_wheel_server_url,
        )
        # Push items onto the stack as we start to resolve their
        # dependencies so at the end we have a list of items that need to
        # be built in order.
        self._build_stack: list[typing.Any] = []
        self._build_requirements: set[tuple[NormalizedName, str]] = set()

        # Track requirements we've seen before so we don't resolve the
        # same dependencies over and over and so we can break cycles in
        # the dependency list. The key is the requirements spec, rather
        # than the package, in case we do have multiple rules for the same
        # package.
        self._seen_requirements: set[SeenKey] = set()

        self._build_order_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "build-order.json"
        self._stack_filename = self.ctx.work_dir / "bootstrap-stack.json"
        logger.info("recording bootstrap stack state to %s", self._stack_filename)

        # Track failed packages in test mode (list of typed dicts for JSON export)
        self.failed_packages: list[FailureRecord] = []

        # Track failed versions in multiple_versions mode
        self._failed_versions: dict[tuple[str, str], Exception] = {}

    @property
    def resolver(self) -> bootstrap_requirement_resolver.BootstrapRequirementResolver:
        """Public accessor for the version resolver."""
        return self._resolver

    def has_failed_version(self, pkg_name: NormalizedName, version: Version) -> bool:
        """Return True if this (pkg_name, version) has previously failed resolution."""
        return (pkg_name, str(version)) in self._failed_versions

    def _resolve_and_add_top_level(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
    ) -> tuple[str, Version] | None:
        """Resolve a top-level requirement and add it to the dependency graph.

        Private method called only by ``bootstrap()``.

        This is the pre-resolution phase before recursive bootstrapping begins.
        In test mode, catches resolution errors and records them as failures.

        When multiple_versions is enabled, resolves and adds all matching versions
        to the graph, but still returns only the first (highest) version for
        backward compatibility.

        Args:
            req: The top-level requirement to resolve.

        Returns:
            Tuple of (source_url, version) if resolution succeeded, None if it
            failed in test mode.

        Raises:
            Exception: In normal mode, re-raises any resolution error.
        """
        try:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            results = self.resolve_versions(
                req=req,
                req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                parent_req=None,
                return_all_versions=self.multiple_versions,
            )
            if self.multiple_versions:
                logger.info(f"resolved {len(results)} version(s) for {req}")

            # Add all resolved versions to the graph
            for source_url, version in results:
                logger.info("%s resolves to %s", req, version)
                self.ctx.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
                    parent_name=None,
                    parent_version=None,
                    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
                    req=req,
                    req_version=version,
                    download_url=source_url,
                    pre_built=pbi.pre_built,
                    constraint=self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name),
                )

            if not results:
                if self.multiple_versions:
                    err = RuntimeError(f"no versions found for {req}")
                    self._record_failed_version(
                        req, "unresolved", err, "no versions resolved, skipping"
                    )
                    if self.test_mode:
                        self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                    return None
                raise RuntimeError(f"Could not resolve any versions for {req}")

            # Return first result for backward compatibility
            return results[0]
        except Exception as err:
            if self.multiple_versions:
                self._record_failed_version(req, "unresolved", err, "failed to resolve")
                if self.test_mode:
                    self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
                return None
            if not self.test_mode:
                raise
            self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, "resolution")
            return None

        req_type: RequirementType,

+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("error_type", [ResolverException, RuntimeError, ValueError])

+    def test_indirect_resolution_error_includes_chain(
+        self,
+        tmp_context: WorkContext,
+        error_type: type[Exception],
+        test_mode: bool,
+        multiple_versions: bool,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Preserve dependency context in raised and recorded resolution failures."""
+        bt = bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(
+            tmp_context, test_mode=test_mode, multiple_versions=multiple_versions
+        )
+        item = _make_resolve_item(
+            req="flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1",
+            why_snapshot=[
+                (RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL, Requirement("its-hub>=1"), Version("1")),
+                (RequirementType.INSTALL, Requirement("reward-hub"), Version("2")),
+                (RequirementType.INSTALL, Requirement("vllm[extra]>=3"), Version("3")),
+            ],
+        )
+        # The current logging/traversal context must not determine the chain.
+        bt.why = [(RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL, Requirement("other"), Version("9"))]
+        err = error_type("resolution failed")
+        expected = (
+            "resolution failed (dependency chain: its-hub==1 -> reward-hub==2"
+            " -> vllm==3 -> flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1)"
+        )
+        expected_type = error_type
+        if error_type is ValueError:
+            expected = f"ValueError: {expected}"
+            expected_type = RuntimeError
+
+        if test_mode or multiple_versions:
+            try:
+                raise err
+            except Exception:
+                assert bt._handle_phase_error(item, err) == []
+            if test_mode:
+                assert bt.failed_packages[0]["exception_message"] == expected
+                assert (
+                    bt.failed_packages[0]["exception_type"] == expected_type.__name__
+                )
+            if multiple_versions:
+                recorded = bt._failed_versions[("flashinfer-python", "unresolved")]

+                assert str(recorded) == expected
+                assert recorded is not err
+        else:
+            with pytest.raises(expected_type) as caught:
+                try:
+                    raise err

checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n
