This document describes the resolution\nstrategies, filtering, and key design decisions.\n\n.. seealso::\n\n   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.\n   :doc:`bootstrapper-architecture` covers how resolution fits into the\n   bootstrap pipeline.\n\nResolution Strategies\n---------------------\n\nDuring bootstrap, the resolver coordinator tries these sources in\npriority order and accumulates results in a thread-safe session cache:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n   │               Resolution Priority Order               │\n   │                                                       │\n   │  1. Session cache (versions found earlier)            │\n   │          │ miss                                       │\n   │          ▼                                            │\n   │  2. Previous dependency graph (prior run)             │\n   │          │ miss                                       │\n   │          ▼                                            │\n   │  3. Network (PyPI / GitHub / GitLab)                  │\n   │     (per-package configurable)                        │\n   │          │ age filter empties result                  │\n   │          ▼                                            │\n   │  4. Cache server fallback                             │\n   │     (multiple_versions mode only)                     │\n   └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\n   Git URL requirements (top-level only) bypass this\n   chain entirely: the repo is cloned and the version\n   is extracted from package metadata.\n\nVersions discovered from any source are merged into the session cache.\nSubsequent requests for the same package skip the network entirely if\nthe cache already contains a matching version.\n\nProvider Hierarchy\n------------------\n\nAll resolution sources inherit from ``BaseProvider``, which implements\nthe resolvelib ``ExtrasProvider`` interface.  The bootstrap engine and\nCLI commands interact with providers through a common\n``find_matches()`` method.\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   BaseProvider\n   ├── PyPIProvider         (PEP 503 Simple API)\n   │   └── PyPICacheProvider  (fromager's own wheel server)\n   ├── GenericProvider      (callback-based, parses tags)\n   │   ├── GitHubTagProvider\n   │   └── GitLabTagProvider\n   └── VersionMapProvider   (pre-resolved version→URL map)\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 25 75\n\n   * - Provider\n     - What it queries\n   * - ``PyPIProvider``\n     - Any PEP 503 Simple API index (pypi.org, custom mirrors).\n       Filters by platform tags, Python version, and yanked status.\n   * - ``PyPICacheProvider``\n     - Subclass of ``PyPIProvider`` pointing at fromager's own wheel\n       server.  No cooldown applied.  Used as a fallback when age\n       filtering eliminates all candidates.\n   * - ``GenericProvider``\n     - Callback-based provider that pairs a version source function\n       with a configurable match function (plain parse or regex).\n       Base class for the tag providers below.\n   * - ``GitHubTagProvider``\n     - GitHub REST API for repository tags.  Versions are parsed\n       from tag names using a configurable pattern.\n   * - ``GitLabTagProvider``\n     - GitLab REST API for repository tags.  Includes upload\n       timestamps for age filtering.\n   * - ``VersionMapProvider``\n     - Wraps a pre-built ``VersionMap`` (version → URL mapping).\n       Used when versions are already known, e.g. from a prior\n       resolution or a settings-provided URL template.\n\nPer-package settings in YAML can select which provider to use and\nconfigure its parameters (index URL, tag pattern, etc.).  Override\nplugins can replace the provider entirely for a specific package via\nthe ``get_resolver_provider`` hook.\n\nVersion Filtering Window\n-------------------------\n\nTwo age-based filters can narrow the set of acceptable versions:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   ◄── too old ──┤  acceptable window  ├── too new ──►\n\n                 │                      │\n            max_age cutoff         cooldown cutoff\n          (reject before this)   (reject after this)\n\n- **Cooldown** rejects releases that are too new.  It ensures a\n  minimum time has passed since publication, guarding against\n  problematic releases.  Configurable per package; bypassed for\n  exact version pins (``==``).\n\n- **Max age** rejects releases that are too old.  Used primarily in\n  ``multiple_versions`` mode to limit the range of versions built.\n\nWhen both are active, only versions published within the window are\nconsidered.  If all candidates are filtered out, the behavior depends\non the mode: in single-version mode a warning is logged and all\ncandidates are kept; in ``multiple_versions`` mode the cache server\nfallback is tried instead.\n\nFlat Resolution by Design\n-------------------------\n\nFromager deliberately does **not** use resolvelib's transitive\ndependency resolution.  Every provider's ``get_dependencies()`` method\nreturns an empty list.  This means resolution is a simple \"find the\nbest matching version\" operation, not a full constraint solver with\nbacktracking.\n\nTransitive dependencies are handled by the bootstrap engine's own DFS\nloop: after a package is built, its install dependencies are extracted\nfrom the wheel metadata and pushed onto the work stack as new\n``RESOLVE`` phase items.  This separation keeps the resolver stateless\nand makes each resolution call independent and thread-safe.\n\nPer-Package Configuration\n-------------------------\n\nPackage settings files (YAML) can configure the resolver for each\npackage independently: resolver type (PyPI, GitHub tags, GitLab tags,\nhook-based, or blocked), index URL, cooldown, tag pattern, and\noverride plugins.\n\nSee :doc:`package-settings` for how settings are loaded and merged.\n    bootstrap_time: datetime.datetime = dataclasses.field(\n        default_factory=lambda: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)\n    )\n\n\n@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, order=True, slots=True, repr=False, kw_only=True)\nclass Candidate:\n    name: str\n    version: Version\n    url: str\n    is_sdist: bool | None = dataclasses.field(default=None)\n    extras: tuple[str, ...] = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)\n    build_tag: BuildTag = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)\n    has_metadata: bool = dataclasses.field(default=False, compare=False)\n    remote_tag: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)\n    remote_commit: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)\n    upload_time: datetime.datetime | None = dataclasses.field(\n        default=None, compare=False\n    )\n\n    _metadata: Metadata | None = dataclasses.field(\n        default=None, init=False, compare=False\n    )\n    _dependencies: list[Requirement] | None = dataclasses.field(\n        default=None, init=False, compare=False\n    )\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        # """Tests for bootstrap_requirement_resolver module."""

from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import resolver
from fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver import BootstrapRequirementResolver
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

# Test fixture: previous dependency graph
old_graph = DependencyGraph()

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("foo"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("foo"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
    req_version=Version("7"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("bar"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("bar"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
    req_version=Version("6"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("blah"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("blah"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
    req_version=Version("5"),
)


def test_resolve_from_graph_no_changes(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver resolves from previous graph with no changes."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Resolving new dependency that doesn't exist in graph
    assert (
        resolver._resolve_from_graph(
            req=Requirement("xyz"),
            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
            pre_built=False,
            parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
        )
        is None
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("7"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_upgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver prefers top-level requirements over history."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr==8
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr==8"),
        req_version=Version("8"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - should get upgraded version from top-level
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("8"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - constraint prevents upgrade
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_downgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver handles version downgrades from top-level requirements."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr<=6
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr<=6"),
        req_version=Version("6"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - gets downgraded to 6
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - already at 6
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_toplevel_dep(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver resolves top-level dependencies correctly."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement for foo
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("foo==2"),
        req_version=Version("2"),
    )

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of bar (no change)
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,

"""Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import (
    candidate,
    constraints,
    context,
    packagesettings,
    resolver,
    sources,
    wheels,
)
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)
_cooldown_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "ccc"},
            "upload-time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_all_recent_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-25T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_COOLDOWN = candidate.Cooldown(
    min_age=_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS,
    bootstrap_time=_BOOTSTRAP_TIME,
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.
    """
    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:
    """Without a cooldown the resolver selects the latest version as normal."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=None)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"


def test_cooldown_all_blocked_raises_informative_error() -> None:
    """When all candidates are within the cooldown window the error says so."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_all_recent_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())

        with pytest.raises(resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException) as exc_info:
            rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "2 candidate(s)" in msg
        assert "published within the last 7 days (release-age cooldown" in msg


def test_cooldown_rejects_candidate_without_upload_time(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A candidate with no upload_time is rejected when a cooldown is active (fail closed)."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    candidate = resolver.Candidate(
        name="test-pkg",
        version=Version("1.0.0"),
        url="https://example.com/test-pkg-1.0.0.tar.gz",
        upload_time=None,
    )
    provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(cooldown=_COOLDOWN)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
        result = provider.is_blocked_by_cooldown(candidate)

    assert result is True
    assert "upload_time unknown" in caplog.text
    assert "1.0.0" in caplog.text

                "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            },
        ],
    }

"""PackageBuildInfo class and system resource helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import pathlib
import types
import typing
from collections.abc import Mapping

import psutil
from packaging.utils import BuildTag, NormalizedName
from packaging.version import Version

from .. import overrides, threading_utils
from ._models import (
    GitOptions,
    PackageSettings,
    ProjectOverride,
    PurlConfig,
    VariantInfo,
)
from ._templates import _resolve_template, substitute_template
from ._typedefs import Annotations, PackageVersion, PatchMap, Template, Variant

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .. import build_environment
    from ._settings import Settings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _default_is_pre_built(*, version: Version, variant: Variant) -> None:
    """Defer pre-built selection to YAML settings."""
    return None


def get_available_memory_gib() -> float:
    """available virtual memory in GiB"""
    return psutil.virtual_memory().available / (1024**3)


class PackageBuildInfo:
    """Package build information

    Public API for PackageSettings with i
    """

    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, ps: PackageSettings) -> None:
        self._variant = typing.cast(Variant, settings.variant)
        self._patches_dir = settings.patches_dir
        self._variant_changelog = settings.variant_changelog()
        self._max_jobs: int | None = settings.max_jobs
        self._ps = ps
        self._plugin_module: types.ModuleType | typing.Literal[False] | None = False
        self._patches: PatchMap | None = None
        self._annotations: Annotations | None = None

    @property
    def package(self) -> NormalizedName:
        """Package name"""
        return typing.cast(NormalizedName, self._ps.name)

    @property
    def variant(self) -> Variant:
        """Variant name"""
        return self._variant

    @property
    def purl_config(self) -> PurlConfig | None:
        """Per-package purl configuration for SBOM generation."""
        return self._ps.purl

    @property
    def annotations(self) -> Annotations:
        """Get Package and variant annotations

        Annotations can be used to attach arbitrary metadata to packages and
        package variants. The feature is inspired by Kubernetes's
        annotations. Variant keys have a higher precedence than package keys.

        The prefix ``fromager.`` is reserved for future use by Fromager.

        ::

           annotations:
             "downstream.maintainer": "Platform Team"
           variants:
             cuda:
               annotations:
                 "downstream.maintainer": "CUDA Accelerator Team"
        """
        if self._annotations is None:
            vi = self._ps.variants.get(self.variant)
            va = vi.annotations if vi is not None else None
            self._annotations = Annotations(self._ps.annotations, va)
        return self._annotations

    @property
    def plugin(self) -> types.ModuleType | None:
        """Get Fromager plugin module"""
        if self._plugin_module is False:
            exts = overrides._get_extensions()
            try:
                mod = exts[self.override_module_name].plugin
                self._plugin_module = typing.cast(types.ModuleType, mod)
            except KeyError:
                self._plugin_module = None
        return self._plugin_module

    def get_all_patches(self) -> PatchMap:
        """Get a mapping of version to list of patches"""

        if self._patches is None:
            patches: PatchMap = {}
            version: Version | None

            # Find unversioned and versioned directories (name + '-' + version)
            # with patches for the package.
            dirs_to_scan = []
            unversioned_dir = self._patches_dir / self.override_module_name
            if unversioned_dir.exists():
                dirs_to_scan.append(unversioned_dir)
            versioned_pattern = f"{self.override_module_name}-*"
            dirs_to_scan.extend(self._patches_dir.glob(versioned_pattern))

            prefix_len = len(self.override_module_name) + 1
            for patchdir in dirs_to_scan:
                if patchdir.name == self.override_module_name:
                    version = None
                else:
                    version = Version(patchdir.name[prefix_len:])
                patches[version] = list(patchdir.glob("*.patch"))
                # variant-specific patches
                patches[version].extend(patchdir.joinpath(self.variant).glob("*.patch"))
                patches[version].sort(key=lambda p: p.name)

            self._patches = patches
        return self._patches

    def get_patches(self, version: Version) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
        """Get patches for a version (and unversioned patches)"""
        # ignore local version for patches
        version = Version(version.public)
        patchfiles: list[pathlib.Path] = []
        patchmap = self.get_all_patches()
        # unversioned patches
        patchfiles.extend(patchmap.get(None, []))
        # version-specific patches
        patchfiles.extend(patchmap.get(version, []))
        # sort by basename
        patchfiles.sort(key=lambda p: p.name)
        return patchfiles

    @property
    def has_config(self) -> bool:
        """Does the package have a config file?"""
        return self._ps.has_config

    @property
    def has_customizations(self) -> bool:
        """Does the package have any customizations?"""
        return bool(
            self.has_config or self.plugin is not None or self.get_all_patches()
        )

    @property
    def pre_built(self) -> bool:
        """Does the variant use pre-build wheels?"""
        return self.is_pre_built()

    def is_pre_built(self, version: Version | None = None) -> bool:
        """Version-aware pre-built check.

        Resolution order:

        1. Plugin hook ``is_pre_built`` (if version given and hook exists)
        2. Version-specific YAML setting
        3. Variant-wide default

        .. versionadded:: 0.95.0
        """
        if version is not None:
            result = overrides.find_and_invoke(
                self.package,
                "is_pre_built",
                _default_is_pre_built,
                version=version,
                variant=self.variant,
            )
            if result is not None:
                return bool(result)
        vi = self._ps.variants.get(self.variant)
        if vi is None:
            return False
        if version is not None:
            pv = typing.cast(PackageVersion, Version(version.public))
            vs = vi.versions.get(pv)
            if vs is not None and vs.pre_built is not None:

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from .. import context, resolver, sources, wheels
from ..requirements_file import RequirementType
from ._phase import Phase
from ._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from ._types import BootstrapPhase

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from ._bootstrapper import Bootstrapper

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _re_resolve_url(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType,
    resolved_version: Version,
    pre_built: bool,
    cache_wheel_server_url: str | None,
) -> str | None:
    """Resolve the pinned version using its selected distribution settings."""
    pinned_req = Requirement(f"{req.name}=={resolved_version}")
    if pre_built:
        wheel_server_urls = wheels.get_wheel_server_urls(
            ctx,
            pinned_req,
            cache_wheel_server_url=cache_wheel_server_url,
            version=resolved_version,
        )
        try:
            url, _ = wheels.resolve_prebuilt_wheel(
                ctx=ctx,
                req=pinned_req,
                wheel_server_urls=wheel_server_urls,
                req_type=req_type,
            )
        except ExceptionGroup:
            return None
        return str(url)

    pbi = ctx.package_build_info(req)
    provider = sources.get_source_provider(
        ctx=ctx,
        req=pinned_req,
        sdist_server_url=pbi.resolver_sdist_server_url(resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL),
        req_type=req_type,
    )
    matches = resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider(provider, pinned_req)
    return str(matches[0][0]) if matches else None


class Start(Phase):
    """Record a resolved requirement in the dependency graph and deduplicate.

    Adds the ``(parent → req)`` edge to the dependency graph, then checks
    whether this ``(req, version)`` pair has already been processed.  Duplicate
    requirements are silently dropped; new ones proceed to source preparation.
    ``tracks_why`` is ``False`` so graph additions happen before the why-stack
    is updated.

    Next phase: ``PrepareSource`` (new requirement) or ``[]`` (already seen).
    """

    phase: typing.ClassVar[BootstrapPhase] = BootstrapPhase.START
    tracks_why: typing.ClassVar[bool] = False

    def run(self, bt: Bootstrapper) -> list[Phase]:
        """START phase: add to graph, check if already seen.

        _track_why is a no-op for this phase (tracks_why is False),
        matching the original behavior where graph addition and
        seen-check happen before pushing onto the why stack.

        Returns:
            Empty list if already seen (nothing to do).
            [PrepareSource] if this is new work.
        """
        wi = self.work_item
        assert wi.resolved_version is not None
        assert wi.source_url is not None

        pbi = bt.ctx.package_build_info(wi.req)
        wi.pbi_pre_built = pbi.is_pre_built(wi.resolved_version)
        if wi.pbi_pre_built != pbi.pre_built or (
            wi.pbi_pre_built
            and pbi.get_wheel_server_url(wi.resolved_version) != pbi.wheel_server_url
        ):
            logger.info(
                "Re-resolving URL for %s==%s with version-specific settings",
                wi.req.name,
                wi.resolved_version,
            )
            url = _re_resolve_url(
                bt.ctx,
                wi.req,
                wi.req_type,
                wi.resolved_version,
                wi.pbi_pre_built,
                bt.cache_wheel_server_url,
            )
            if url is not None:
                wi.source_url = url
            else:
                logger.warning(
                    "Could not re-resolve URL for %s==%s; keeping original URL %s",
                    wi.req.name,
                    wi.resolved_version,
                    wi.source_url,
                )

        # Add to graph (skip TOP_LEVEL, already added in _resolve_and_add_top_level)
        if wi.req_type != RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL:
            bt.add_to_graph(
                wi.req,
                wi.req_type,
                wi.resolved_version,
                wi.source_url,
                wi.parent,
            )

        wi.build_sdist_only = bt.sdist_only and not wi.is_build_requirement_context()

        if bt.has_been_seen(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, wi.build_sdist_only):
            logger.debug(
                f"redundant {wi.req_type} dependency {wi.req} "
                f"({wi.resolved_version}, sdist_only={wi.build_sdist_only}) "
                f"for {bt.explain}"
            )
            return []
        bt.mark_as_seen(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, wi.build_sdist_only)

        logger.info(
            f"new {wi.req_type} dependency {wi.req} resolves to {wi.resolved_version}"
        )

        wi.exclusive_build = pbi.exclusive_build
        return [PrepareSource(wi)]

Hooks and Overrides
===================

Fromager has two plugin systems that serve different purposes:
**per-package overrides** replace default behavior for a specific
package, while **global hooks** broadcast notifications after events
for every package.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.
   :doc:`/reference/hooks` documents each override hook's arguments and
   return values.  :doc:`/customization` covers global hooks with code
   examples.

Comparison
----------

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 20 40 40

   * - Aspect
     - Per-Package Overrides
     - Global Hooks
   * - **Scope**
     - One named package
     - Every package
   * - **Cardinality**
     - At most one override module per package
     - Multiple plugins per hook
   * - **Semantics**
     - Replaces the default implementation
     - Runs in addition to the default
   * - **Return value**
     - Used by the caller
     - None (fire-and-forget)
   * - **Typical use**
     - Custom download, build, or resolution logic
     - Publishing wheels, validation, logging

Per-Package Overrides
---------------------

An override module provides alternative implementations for specific
build steps.  Fromager looks up the module by the canonicalized package
name.  If the module defines the requested method, it is called instead
of the default; otherwise the default runs.

Override hooks cover resolution, source acquisition, building,
dependency extraction, and build environment customization.  Third-party
packages register overrides via the ``fromager.project_overrides``
entry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a package name to
a Python module.

See :doc:`/reference/hooks` for the complete list of hooks and their
arguments.

Version-Aware Pre-Built Selection
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

.. versionadded:: 0.95.0

A package override can define ``is_pre_built(*, version, variant)``.
Return ``True`` to select a pre-built wheel, ``False`` to select source,
or ``None`` to defer to YAML settings. The hook receives the resolved
``Version`` (including any local segment) and the active variant.
It runs only when a version is supplied to
``PackageBuildInfo.is_pre_built()``; querying the variant default does
not invoke it. A non-``None`` result takes precedence over YAML.

When the result differs from the variant default, the bootstrapper
re-resolves the pinned version's URL before recording dependency edges.
Version-specific wheel server changes also trigger re-resolution.
See :doc:`package-settings` for settings precedence and fallback behavior.

Global Hooks
------------

Global hooks are event callbacks that fire for every package.  All
registered plugins for a hook are called sequentially.  They cannot
alter the build result — they are purely side-effecting notifications.

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 75

   * - Hook
     - When it fires
   * - ``post_build``
     - After a wheel is built from source (not for prebuilt wheels)
   * - ``prebuilt_wheel``
     - After a prebuilt wheel is downloaded (not built from source)
   * - ``post_bootstrap``
     - After a package is bootstrapped, before its install dependencies
       are processed

Third-party packages register hooks via the ``fromager.hooks``
entry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a hook name to
a callable.

See :doc:`/customization` for examples and argument details.

Package Settings
================

Fromager uses a layered settings system to configure how each package
is resolved, downloaded, patched, and built.  Settings flow from YAML
files on disk through a merge pipeline into a single facade object
used by the build pipeline.

.. seealso::

   :doc:`/reference/config-reference` documents every configuration
   field.  :doc:`architecture-overview` maps the major subsystems.

Settings Loading Flow
---------------------

.. code-block:: text

   CLI flags
   (--settings-file, --settings-dir, --patches-dir)
         │
         ▼
   Settings.from_files()
   ├── Load settings.yaml ──► SettingsFile (global config)
   └── Glob settings/*.yaml ──► PackageSettings (one per package)
         │
         ▼
   Settings object (held by WorkContext)
         │
         │  package_build_info("torch")  (on demand, cached)
         ▼
   PackageBuildInfo
   (single facade used by the build pipeline)

``PackageBuildInfo`` objects are created lazily the first time a
package is queried and cached for the rest of the run.

Directory Structure
-------------------

.. code-block:: text

   overrides/
   ├── settings.yaml              # Global settings
   ├── settings/                  # Per-package settings
   │   ├── torch.yaml
   │   ├── flash-attn.yaml
   │   └── ...
   └── patches/                   # Patches
       ├── torch/                 # Unversioned (all versions)
       │   ├── 001-fix.patch
       │   └── cpu/               # Variant-specific
       │       └── 002-cpu.patch
       └── torch-2.4.0/           # Version-specific
           └── 001-ver.patch

Package YAML filenames use the canonicalized package name (lowercase,
hyphens).  All three directories are configurable via CLI flags.

Merge Order
-----------

Settings are merged from least-specific to most-specific.  Later
layers override earlier ones:

.. code-block:: text

   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  1. Pydantic field defaults                      │
   │     (empty env, default build options, etc.)     │
   │                                                  │
   │  2. Global settings.yaml                         │
   │     (SBOM config, global changelog)              │
   │                                                  │
   │  3. Per-package YAML file                        │
   │     (env, resolver, build options, patches, ...) │
   │                                                  │
   │  4. Variant overrides (within package YAML)      │
   │     (env vars, pre_built, wheel_server_url)      │
   │                                                  │
   │  5. Version-specific patches and changelog       │
   │     (patches/<pkg>-<version>/, changelog entries)│
   │                                                  │
   │  6. Override plugin hooks (runtime)              │
   │     (update_extra_environ can mutate env vars)   │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

For environment variables specifically, the merge order within a
single ``get_extra_environ()`` call is: parallel-jobs settings, build
environment paths, package-level ``env``, then variant-level ``env``.
Entries can reference earlier values using ``$VAR`` template syntax.

PackageBuildInfo Facade
-----------------------

``PackageBuildInfo`` is the single interface the build pipeline uses to
query all package configuration.  It wraps a ``PackageSettings`` and
adds variant awareness, patch discovery, and template resolution.

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 1
   :widths: 25 75

   * - Category
     - What it provides
   * - **Identity**
     - Package name, variant, whether a config file exists, override
       plugin module
   * - **Resolution**
     - Sdist server URL, include wheels/sdists flags, platform
       filtering, per-package cooldown override
   * - **Build config**
     - Environment variables, parallel jobs, exclusive build flag,
       PEP 517 config settings, build directory
   * - **Source**
     - Download URL and filename templates with ``${version}``
       substitution, git submodule options
   * - **Patches**
     - Merged list of unversioned + version-specific + variant-specific
       patch files, sorted by filename
   * - **Metadata**
     - Build tag (from changelog length), annotations, PURL config,
       pyproject.toml overrides

See :doc:`/reference/config-reference` for the full field reference.


Version-Specific Distribution Settings
-------------------------------------

.. versionadded:: 0.95.0

Set ``pre_built`` and ``wheel_server_url`` under
``variants.<variant>.versions.<version>`` to override the variant defaults.
Omitted fields inherit the defaults; an omitted or bare ``versions:`` key
defines no overrides. Version lookup ignores local segments, so
``2.8.0+cpu`` uses the settings for ``2.8.0``.

``PackageBuildInfo.is_pre_built(version)`` checks the override hook first,
then version-specific YAML, then the variant default.
``get_wheel_server_url(version)`` checks version-specific YAML before the
variant default. Their properties, ``pre_built`` and ``wheel_server_url``,
return the defaults without invoking the hook.

After resolving a version, the bootstrapper's START phase re-resolves its
URL if the pre-built choice changes or a pre-built version uses a different
wheel server. Resolution pins the full version, including its local segment.
The corrected URL is recorded before graph insertion and duplicate detection.
If no replacement is found, Fromager warns and retains the original URL.

+variant default. Their properties, ``pre_built`` and ``wheel_server_url``,
+return the defaults without invoking the hook.
+
+After resolving a version, the bootstrapper's START phase re-resolves its
+URL if the pre-built choice changes or a pre-built version uses a different
+wheel server. Resolution pins the full version, including its local segment.
+The corrected URL is recorded before graph insertion and duplicate detection.
+If no replacement is found, Fromager warns and retains the original URL.

Prefer regression tests for bugs\n  involving retries, rate limits, authentication, external APIs, and response\n  mapping.\n- Track long-running development servers with PID files or equivalent logs, report\n  their URLs, and stop them when requested.\n- Report exact changed files, validation results, environmental limitations, and any\n  follow-up needed. Do not claim an integration test passed if its runtime\n  dependency was unavailable.\n# Writing and Python\n\n- Never use em-dashes. Use normal punctuation or connective words instead.\n- Use module-level Python imports unless a function-level import is necessary to\n  avoid a circular dependency.\n# Codex Runtime Behavior\n\nThis page applies only to Codex. All non-Codex runtimes must ignore it.\n\nUse the `caveman:caveman` skill in lite mode for all sessions and user-facing chat\nresponses by default. Keep responses concise, but use complete grammatical\nsentences and retain articles. Preserve exact code, commands, errors, numbers,\nnegations, and technical terms. Use normal prose in code comments, commits,\ndocumentation, issues, reviews, and other text written for third parties. Use full\nor ultra mode only when the user explicitly requests it. Stop or change this mode\nwhen the user requests `normal mode`, `stop caveman`, or a different Caveman\nintensity.\n# Contributing to Fromager\n\nFromager thrives on practical, well-tested contributions. This guide summarizes how to set up a workspace, follow our standards, and submit polished changes. Skim it once, keep it handy, and refer back whenever you are unsure.\n\n> **Note**: If you're using AI coding assistants, also see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI-optimized quick reference.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Quick Start](#quick-start)\n- [Coding Standards](#coding-standards)\n- [Testing](#testing)\n- [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines)\n- [Before Submitting](#before-submitting)\n- [Design Patterns Used in Fromager](#design-patterns-used-in-fromager)\n- [Quick Reference](#quick-reference)\n- [Getting Help](#getting-help)\n- [Resources](#resources)\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.12 or newer\n\n- `hatch` for environment and task management\n\n  ```bash\n  pip install hatch\n  # or\n  pipx install hatch  # recommended\n  ```\n\n### Initial Setup\n\n```bash\n# 1. Fork the repository on GitHub\n# 2. Clone your fork\ngit clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fromager.git\ncd fromager\n\n# 3. Add upstream remote\ngit remote add upstream https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager.git\n\n# 4. Create development environment\nhatch env create\n\n# 5. Install pre-commit hooks (optional but recommended)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n```\n\n### Contribution Workflow\n\n```bash\n# 1. Sync with upstream\ngit checkout main\ngit fetch upstream\ngit merge upstream/main\n\n# 2. Create a feature branch\ngit checkout -b feat/<short-description>\n\n# 3. Make changes and test as you go\nhatch run test:test tests/test_<module>.py       # Test your specific changes\n\n# 4. Before committing, run full quality checks\nhatch run lint:precommit\n\n# 5. Commit using Conventional Commits\ngit commit -m \"feat(scope): short summary\"\n\n# 6. Push to your fork\ngit push origin feat/<short-description>\n\n# 7. Create a pull request on GitHub\n```\n\n### Pre-commit Hook (Recommended)\n\nTo ensure quality checks run automatically before each commit, install the pre-commit hooks that run linting, mypy type checking, and commit message validation:\n\n```bash\n# Install pre-commit hooks (run once after cloning)\nhatch run lint:install-hooks\n\n# The hooks automatically run linters before each commit and validate\n# that commit messages follow Conventional Commits format.\n\n# If a hook fails, it will prevent the commit and show helpful messages.\n# You can fix formatting issues automatically with:\nhatch run lint:fix\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hooks prevent commits that would fail CI quality checks, and enforce that all commit messages follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format documented in the [Commit Guidelines](#commit-guidelines) section.\n\n---\n\n## Coding Standards\n\n### Type Annotations\n\n- Every function (including tests) must annotate all parameters and return values.\n- Use modern `X | None` syntax instead of `Optional[X]` (PEP 604).\n- Prefer precise collection types (`list[str]`, `dict[str, int]`, etc.).\n\n```python\ndef process(data: str | None, count: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Process the input and return aggregate counts.\"\"\"\n    return {}\n```\n\n### Code Quality and Formatting\n\n- Ruff enforces both formatting and linting.\n- Run `hatch run lint:fix` to automatically format code.\n- See [Quick Reference](#quick-reference) for additional commands.\n\n### Import Organization\n\n- **PEP 8: imports should be at the top**: All import statements must be placed at the top of the file, after module docstrings and before other code.\n- **No local imports**: Do not place import statements inside functions, methods, or conditional blocks.\n\n### Documentation Expectations\n\n- Add a module docstring describing purpose and high-level behavior.\n- Public functions and classes require docstrings that cover arguments, return values, and noteworthy behavior.\n- Keep prose short and imperative; explain \"why\" decisions when the code itself cannot.\n\n```python\ndef retry_on_exception(\n    exceptions: tuple[type[Exception], ...],\n    max_attempts: int = 5,\n) -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Retry decorated call on the provided exception types.\n\n    Args:\n        exceptions: Exception types that trigger a retry.\n        max_attempts: Maximum number of attempts.\n\n    Returns:\n        Decorator function.\n    \"\"\"\n    ...\n```\n\n### Commenting Guidelines\n\n- Write self-explanatory code; reserve comments for non-obvious intent or domain context.\n- Capture reasoning, invariants, or unexpected trade-offs—never repeat the code literally.\n\n```python\n# Bad - comment just repeats the code\nx = x + 1  # increment x\n\n# Good - clear variable name makes the comment unnecessary\ntotal_attempts += 1\n\n# Good - comment explains the reasoning behind the approach\n# Exponential backoff avoids thundering herd when many jobs retry at once.\nwait_time = min(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1), max_backoff)\n```\n\n### Logging\n\n- Use a module-level logger and the appropriate log level for the situation.\n- When processing per-requirement work, wrap nested calls in `req_ctxvar_context()` so log records automatically include the package (and optional version). This keeps CLI logs searchable even when work runs in parallel.\n\n```python\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\ndef sync_artifacts() -> None:\n    logger.info(\"Starting artifact sync\")\n    logger.debug(\"Artifacts queued: %s\", pending_jobs)\n\n# When processing a specific package, wrap calls to include package info in logs\n# req: Requirement object for the package being processed\n# version: Version string being built (optional)\nwith req_ctxvar_context(req, version):\n    logger.info(\"Resolving build dependencies\")  # Logs will include package name\n```\n\n### Error Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run test:test tests/test_context.py        # Specific file\nhatch run test:test --log-level DEBUG            # Verbose output\nhatch run test:coverage-report                   # Coverage summary\n```\n\n---\n\n## Commit Guidelines\n\nFromager follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/).\n\n```text\n<type>(<scope>): <short summary>\n\n<body explaining what + why>\n\n<footer for metadata>\n```\n\n### Common Types\n\n- `feat`: new functionality\n- `fix`: bug fix\n- `docs`: documentation only\n- `test`: tests only\n- `refactor`: behavioral no-op refactor\n- `perf`: performance improvement\n- `chore`: tooling or dependency change\n\n### Writing Tips\n\n- Subject ≤ 72 characters, imperative voice, no trailing period.\n- Describe motivation in the body if the diff is not self-explanatory.\n- Reference issues when relevant (`Closes: #123`).\n\n### Examples\n\n```text\nfeat(http_retry): add exponential backoff with jitter\n\nSupport transient failures more gracefully by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCloses: #456\n```\n\n```text\nfix(constraints): handle missing constraint file gracefully\n\nValidate file existence and emit a helpful message instead of crashing.\n```\n\n### AI-Generated Code Attribution\n\nWhen AI tools create or significantly modify code, add attribution:\n\n```text\nfeat(resolver): add exponential backoff for HTTP retries\n\nImproves resilience when PyPI is under load by adding jittered backoff.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>\nCloses: #456\n```\n\nAvoid vague messages like `fix bug`, `update files`, or `WIP`.\n\n---\n\n## Before Submitting\n\n### Quality Checklist\n\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:fix`\n- [ ] `hatch run test:test`\n- [ ] `hatch run mypy:check`\n- [ ] `hatch run lint:check`\n\n### Code Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Every function is fully typed.\n- [ ] Public APIs include docstrings.\n- [ ] Tests cover the change (positive + edge cases).\n- [ ] No trailing whitespace; files end with a newline.\n- [ ] Conventional Commit format followed.\n- [ ] Code aligns with existing patterns.\n\n---\n\n## Design Patterns Used in Fromager\n\n### Context Managers\n\n```python\n@contextlib.contextmanager\ndef resource_context() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n    \"\"\"Manage resource lifecycle.\"\"\"\n    setup_resource()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        cleanup_resource()\n```\n\n### Thread-Safe Decorators\n\n```python\ndef with_thread_lock() -> typing.Callable:\n    \"\"\"Create thread-safe wrapper.\"\"\"\n    lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def decorator(func: typing.Callable) -> typing.Callable:\n        @functools.wraps(func)\n        def wrapper(*args: typing.Any, **kwargs: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:\n            with lock:\n                return func(*args, **kwargs)\n        return wrapper\n    return decorator\n```\n\n### Pydantic Validation\n\n```python\ndef _validate_envkey(value: typing.Any) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Normalize environment variable keys.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, bool):\n        return \"1\" if value else \"0\"\n    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):\n        return str(value)\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        return value.strip()\n    raise TypeError(f\"unsupported type {type(value)}: {value!r}\")\n\nEnvKey = typing.Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_validate_envkey)]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Commands\n\n| Task | Command |\n| -- | -- |\n| Run tests | `hatch run test:test` |\n| Check code quality | `hatch run lint:check` |\n| Fix formatting | `hatch run lint:fix` |\n| Type checking | `hatch run mypy:check` |\n\n### Standards\n\n| Standard | Requirement |\n| -- | -- |\n| Type annotations | Required for every function |\n| Docstrings | Required on public APIs |\n| Tests | Required for new behavior |\n| Trailing whitespace | Forbidden |\n| File endings | Single newline |\n| Commit format | Conventional Commits |\n\n---\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for discussion or questions or design proposals.\n- File an issue with a minimal reproduction for bugs.\n- Ask for targeted feedback directly in your pull request.\n\n## Resources\n\n- [PEP 8 - Style Guide](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008/)\n- [PEP 484 - Type Hints](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0484/)\n- [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n- [pytest Documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [Ruff Documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)\n\n---\n\n**Thanks for contributing to Fromager!** If you spot gaps or have suggestions for this guide, open an issue or start a discussion—we love improving our contributor experience.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? Make it a full sentence.\nAGENTS.md\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport typing\n\nfrom ..requirements_file import RequirementType\nfrom ._phase import Phase\nfrom ._prepare_source import PrepareSource\nfrom ._types import BootstrapPhase\n\nif typing.TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from ._bootstrapper import Bootstrapper\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass Start(Phase):\n    \"\"\"Record a resolved requirement in the dependency graph and deduplicate.\n\n    Adds the ``(parent → req)`` edge to the dependency graph, then checks\n    whether this ``(req, version)`` pair has already been processed.  Duplicate\n    requirements are silently dropped; new ones proceed to source preparation.\n    ``tracks_why`` is ``False`` so graph additions happen before the why-stack\n    is updated.\n\n    Next phase: ``PrepareSource`` (new requirement) or ``[]`` (already seen).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    phase: typing.ClassVar[BootstrapPhase] = BootstrapPhase.START\n    tracks_why: typing.ClassVar[bool] = False\n\n    def run(self, bt: Bootstrapper) -> list[Phase]:\n        \"\"\"START phase: add to graph, check if already seen.\n\n        _track_why is a no-op for this phase (tracks_why is False),\n        matching the original behavior where graph addition and\n        seen-check happen before pushing onto the why stack.\n\n        Returns:\n            Empty list if already seen (nothing to do).\n            [PrepareSource] if this is new work.\n        \"\"\"\n        wi = self.work_item\n        assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n        assert wi.source_url is not None\n\n        # Add to graph (skip TOP_LEVEL, already added in _resolve_and_add_top_level)\n        if wi.req_type != RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL:\n            bt.add_to_graph(\n                wi.req,\n                wi.req_type,\n                wi.resolved_version,\n                wi.source_url,\n                wi.parent,\n            )\n\n        wi.build_sdist_only = bt.sdist_only and not wi.is_build_requirement_context()\n\n        if bt.has_been_seen(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, wi.build_sdist_only):\n            logger.debug(\n                f\"redundant {wi.req_type} dependency {wi.req} \"\n                f\"({wi.resolved_version}, sdist_only={wi.build_sdist_only}) \"\n                f\"for {bt.explain}\"\n            )\n            return []\n        bt.mark_as_seen(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, wi.build_sdist_only)\n\n        logger.info(\n            f\"new {wi.req_type} dependency {wi.req} resolves to {wi.resolved_version}\"\n        )\n\n        # Must set pbi_pre_built before constructing PrepareSource so that\n        # PrepareSource.background_work() immediately sees the correct value.\n        pbi = bt.ctx.package_build_info(wi.req)\n        wi.pbi_pre_built = pbi.is_pre_built(wi.resolved_version)\n        wi.exclusive_build = pbi.exclusive_build\n        return [PrepareSource(wi)]\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Later\nlayers override earlier ones:\n\n.. code-block:: text\n\n   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n   │  1. Pydantic field defaults                      │\n   │     (empty env, default build options, etc.)     │\n   │                                                  │\n   │  2. Global settings.yaml                         │\n   │     (SBOM config, global changelog)              │\n   │                                                  │\n   │  3. Version-specific patches and changelog       │\n   │     (patches/<pkg>-<version>/, changelog entries)│\n   │                                                  │\n   │  6. Override plugin hooks (runtime)              │\n   │     (update_extra_environ can mutate env vars)   │\n   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\nFor environment variables specifically, the merge order within a\nsingle ``get_extra_environ()`` call is: parallel-jobs settings, build\nenvironment paths, package-level ``env``, then variant-level ``env``.\nEntries can reference earlier values using ``$VAR`` template syntax.\n\nPackageBuildInfo Facade\n-----------------------\n\n``PackageBuildInfo`` is the single interface the build pipeline uses to\nquery all package configuration.  It wraps a ``PackageSettings`` and\nadds variant awareness, patch discovery, and template resolution.\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 25 75\n\n   * - Category\n     - What it provides\n   * - **Identity**\n     - Package name, variant, whether a config file exists, override\n       plugin module\n   * - **Resolution**\n     - Sdist server URL, include wheels/sdists flags, platform\n       filtering, per-package cooldown override\n   * - **Build config**\n     - Environment variables, parallel jobs, exclusive build flag,\n       PEP 517 config settings, build directory\n   * - **Source**\n     - Download URL and filename templates with ``${version}``\n       substitution, git submodule options\n   * - **Patches**\n     - Merged list of unversioned + version-specific + variant-specific\n       patch files, sorted by filename\n   * - **Metadata**\n     - Build tag (from changelog length), annotations, PURL config,\n       pyproject.toml overrides\n\nSee :doc:`/reference/config-reference` for the full field reference.\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 20 40 40\n\n   * - Aspect\n     - Per-Package Overrides\n     - Global Hooks\n   * - **Scope**\n     - One named package\n     - Every package\n   * - **Cardinality**\n     - At most one override module per package\n     - Multiple plugins per hook\n   * - **Semantics**\n     - Replaces the default implementation\n     - Runs in addition to the default\n   * - **Return value**\n     - Used by the caller\n     - None (fire-and-forget)\n   * - **Typical use**\n     - Custom download, build, or resolution logic\n     - Publishing wheels, validation, logging\n\nPer-Package Overrides\n---------------------\n\nAn override module provides alternative implementations for specific\nbuild steps.  Fromager looks up the module by the canonicalized package\nname.  If the module defines the requested method, it is called instead\nof the default; otherwise the default runs.\n\nOverride hooks cover resolution, source acquisition, building,\ndependency extraction, and build environment customization.  Third-party\npackages register overrides via the ``fromager.project_overrides``\nentry-point group in their ``pyproject.toml``, mapping a package name to\na Python module.\n\nSee :doc:`/reference/hooks` for the complete list of hooks and their\narguments.\n\nGlobal Hooks\n------------\n\nGlobal hooks are event callbacks that fire for every package.  All\nregistered plugins for a hook are called sequentially.  They cannot\nalter the build result — they are purely side-effecting notifications.\n\n.. list-table::\n   :header-rows: 1\n   :widths: 25 75\n\n   * - Hook\n     - When it fires\n   * - ``post_build``\n     - After a wheel is built from source (not for prebuilt wheels)\n   * - ``prebuilt_wheel``\n     - After a prebuilt wheel is downloaded (not built from source)\n   * - ``post_bootstrap``\n     - After a package is bootstrapped, before its install dependencies\n       are processed\n\nThird-party packages register hooks via the ``fromager.hooks``\nentry-point group {"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"item_15","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc \"python - <<'PY'\nfrom pathlib import Path\np=Path('src/fromager/packagesettings/_pbi.py')\ns=p.read_text()\npos=s.index('    def get_changelog')\ns=s[:pos]+s[pos:].replace('pv = typing.cast(PackageVersion, Version(version.public))', 'pv = typing.cast(PackageVersion, version)')\np.write_text(s)\np=Path('docs/concepts/package-settings.rst')\ns=p.read_text()+'''\n\nVersion-Specific Distribution Settings\n-------------------------------------\n\n.. versionadded:: 0.95.0\n\nSet \"'``pre_built`` and ``wheel_server_url`` under\n``variants.<variant>.versions.<version>`` to override the variant defaults.\nOmitted fields inherit the defaults; an omitted or bare ``versions:`` key\ndefines no overrides. Version lookup ignores local segments, so\n``2.8.0+cpu`` uses the settings for ``2.8.0``.\n\n``PackageBuildInfo.is_pre_built(version)`` checks the override hook first,\nthen version-specific YAML, then the variant default.\n``get_wheel_server_url(version)`` checks version-specific YAML before the\nvariant default. Their properties, ``pre_built`` and ``wheel_server_url``,\nreturn the defaults without invoking the hook.\n\nAfter resolving a version, the bootstrapper'\"'s START phase re-resolves its\nURL if the pre-built choice changes or a pre-built version uses a different\nwheel server. Resolution pins the full version, including its local segment.\nThe corrected URL is recorded before graph insertion and duplicate detection.\nIf no replacement is found, Fromager warns and retains the original URL.\n'''\np.write_text(s)\np=Path('docs/concepts/hooks-and-overrides.rst')\ns=p.read_text().replace('Global Hooks\\\\n------------','''Version-Aware Pre-Built Selection\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\n.. versionadded:: 0.95.0\n\nA package override can define \"'``is_pre_built(*, version, variant)``.\nReturn ``True`` to select a pre-built wheel, ``False`` to select source,\nor ``None`` to defer to YAML settings. The hook receives the resolved\n``Version`` (including any local segment) and the active variant.\nIt runs only when a version is supplied to\n``PackageBuildInfo.is_pre_built()``; querying the variant default does\nnot invoke it. A non-``None`` result takes precedence over YAML.\n\nWhen the result differs from the variant default, the bootstrapper\nre-resolves the pinned version'\"'s URL before recording dependency edges.\nVersion-specific wheel server changes also trigger re-resolution.\nSee :doc:\"'`package-settings` for settings precedence and fallback behavior.\n\nGlobal Hooks\n------------'\"''')\np.write_text(s)\nPY\nhatch run lint:fix src/fromager/packagesettings/_pbi.py src/fromager/bootstrapper/_start.py src/fromager/wheels.py tests/test_packagesettings.py tests/test_bootstrapper_iterative.py\"","aggregated_output":"","exit_code":null,"status":"in_progress"}}

str(matches[0][0]) if matches else None\n\n\nclass Start(Phase):\n    \"\"\"Record a resolved requirement in the dependency graph and deduplicate.\n\n    Adds the ``(parent → req)`` edge to the """Tests for the iterative bootstrap implementation.

Tests cover:
- Phase class hierarchy: class variables and base class behavior
- WorkItem dataclass defaults and state accumulation
- _track_why context manager behavior
- create_unresolved_work_items helper
- Resolve.run() version expansion
- Start.run() graph addition and seen-check
- PrepareSource.run() all branches (prebuilt, source, cached, bad path)
- PrepareBuild.run() dep installation and extraction
- Build.run() conditional install and result construction
- ProcessInstallDeps.run() hooks, dep extraction, error modes
- Complete.run() cleanup
- _handle_phase_error for all three error modes
- End-to-end iterative loop with LIFO ordering
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import logging
import pathlib
import typing
from unittest.mock import Mock, call, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from fromager import bootstrapper, build_environment
from fromager.bootstrapper._build import Build
from fromager.bootstrapper._complete import Complete
from fromager.bootstrapper._phase import Phase
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from fromager.bootstrapper._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from fromager.bootstrapper._resolve import Resolve
from fromager.bootstrapper._start import Start, _re_resolve_url
from fromager.bootstrapper._types import (
    BootstrapPhase,
    PreparedSourceData,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from fromager.bootstrapper._work_item import WorkItem
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType


def _make_resolved_future(
    result: typing.Any,
) -> concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any]:
    """Return an already-completed Future carrying *result*."""
    future: concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any] = concurrent.futures.Future()
    future.set_result(result)
    return future


def _make_work_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> WorkItem:
    return WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=req_type,
        why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
        parent=parent,
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version) if version else None,
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )


def _make_resolve_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Resolve:
    return Resolve(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
        )
    )


def _make_start_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    version: str = "1.0",
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Start:
    return Start(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
            source_url=source_url,
            resolved_version=Version(version),
        )
    )


_PHASE_TO_CLASS: dict[BootstrapPhase, type[Phase]] = {
    BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE: Resolve,
    BootstrapPhase.START: Start,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE: PrepareSource,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD: PrepareBuild,
    BootstrapPhase.BUILD: Build,
    BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS: ProcessInstallDeps,
    BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE: Complete,
}


def _make_build_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    version: str = "1.0",
    phase: BootstrapPhase = BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> Phase:
    wi = WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        why_snapshot=[],
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version),
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )
    return _PHASE_TO_CLASS[phase](wi)


class TestPhaseClassVariables:
    """Verify class-variable declarations on each Phase subclass."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "cls, expected_phase, expected_tracks_why",
        [
            (Resolve, BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE, False),
            (Start, BootstrapPhase.START, False),
            (PrepareSource, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE, True),
            (PrepareBuild, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD, True),
            (Build, BootstrapPhase.BUILD, True),
            (ProcessInstallDeps, BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS, True),
            (Complete, BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE, True),
        ],
    )
